subject: Inference on Multivariate Gaussian Process model?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Inference on Multivariate Gaussian Process model?
parts:
I'm about to start working on the inference for a multivariate Gaussian Process model, and I thought I'd first check: has anyone else has written any code for this yet?

I see that gp-multi-sim.stan in the example repo implements simulation from such models, but I'm trying to wrap my head around how to structure the input data and stan code to achieve inference instead of simulation. If anyone has had a crack at it already, I'd be much obliged to see how it's done.

Cheers,

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Inference on Multivariate Gaussian Process model?
parts:
I managed to work it out. Below is Stan code followed by R demo. The only issue now is that when I tweak the example to have multiple observations at each point on one of the predictor dimensions  (in the R code, set reps to >1 on line 11), things slow down considerably and I can't think of how to apply the trick I posted in another thread (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/GXgpg7C0QAM) to deal with such predictor repetition efficiently. Any thoughts on this? Most of my data is of the multivariate kind with lots of predictor repetition (ex. 2s of 1Khz eeg, measured 30 times in each of 2 conditions), which will surely choke the standard approach below.

#file: gp-multi-fit.stan
  data {
    #N: number of data points
    int<lower=1> N ; 
    #D: number of predictors
    int<lower=1> D ; 
    #X: predictor matrix
    matrix[N,D] X ; 
    #Y: vector of data
    vector[N] Y ;
  }
  transformed data {
    #mu: set to zero for mean-reverting behaviour
    vector[N] mu ; 
    for (n in 1:N){
      mu[n] <- 0 ;
    }
  }
  parameters {
    #eta_sq: scale of output (Y)
    real<lower=0> eta_sq ;
    #inv_rho_sq: x-axis scale of influence between points, unique for each 
    #    dimension of the predictor matrix
    vector<lower=0>[D] inv_rho_sq ;
    #sigma_sq: noise scale
    real<lower=0> sigma_sq ;
  }
  transformed parameters{
    #Sigma: covariance matrix
    matrix[N,N] Sigma ;
    { #nest scope to ensure temp isn't saved as a parameter
      #temp: temporary accumulator of squared euclidean distances
      vector[D] temp ;
      # Compute Sigma off-diagonals
      for (i in 1:(N-1)) {
        for (j in (i+1):N) {
          #next loop is supposed to be achieved by dot_self(), but I couldn't get 
          #that to work, so went with an accumulator then summing
          for(d in 1:D){
            temp[d] <-  pow(X[i,d] - X[j,d],2)/inv_rho_sq[d] ;
          }
          Sigma[i,j] <- eta_sq * exp(-sum(temp)) ;
          Sigma[j,i] <- Sigma[i,j] ; #lower mirrors upper
        }
      }
      # Compute Sigma diagonals 
      for (k in 1:N){
        Sigma[k,k] <- eta_sq + sigma_sq ; # sigma_sq adds "jitter"
      }
    }
  }
  model {
    #priors on kernel parameters
    eta_sq ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    inv_rho_sq ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    sigma_sq ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    #assert Y as sampled from multivariate normal
    Y ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma) ;
  }
  generated quantities {
    vector[N] mu_preds ;
    vector[N] y_preds ;
    {
      matrix[N,N] L ;
      matrix[N,N] K ;
      matrix[N,N] K_transpose_div_Sigma ;
      matrix[N,N] Tau ;

      K <- Sigma ;
   
      #Modify K's diagonals to exclude sigma_sq
      for (n in 1:N){
        K[n,n] <- eta_sq ;
      }

      K_transpose_div_Sigma <- K' / Sigma ;
      mu_preds <- K_transpose_div_Sigma * Y ;
      Tau <- Sigma - K_transpose_div_Sigma * K ;

      #make sure Tau is symmetric
      for (i in 1:(N-1)){
        for (j in (i+1):N){
          Tau[i,j] <- Tau[j,i] ;
        }
      }

      L <- cholesky_decompose(Tau) ;
      y_preds <- multi_normal_cholesky_rng(mu_preds, L) ;
    }

  }


And now some data generating, visualization, fitting, and more visualization R code:

  set.seed(1)
  N = 100
  x = seq(-10,10,length.out=N)
  y_true = sin(x)*dnorm(x,5,8)
  y2a = y_true + dnorm(x,-5,2)/5
  y2b = y_true - dnorm(x,-5,2)/5
  plot(x,y_true,ylim=c(min(y2b),max(y2a)))
  lines(x,y2a)
  lines(x,y2b)

  reps = 1
  y2 = c(y2a,y2b)
  y2 = scale(y2)[,1] #normalize
  y2 = rep(y2,times=reps)
  y2 = y2+rnorm(length(y2),0,.5)

  x2 = rep(x,times=reps*2)
  x2 = (x2-min(x2))/(diff(range(x2))) #rescale to 0-1


  group = rep(c(.5,-.5),each=N,times=reps)
  dat = data.frame(
      x = x2
      , y = y2
      , group = group
      , rep_num = rep(1:reps,each=N*2)
  )

  p = ggplot()
  p = p + geom_point(
      data = dat
      , mapping = aes(
          x = x
          , y = y
          , colour = factor(group)
      )
      , alpha = .5
  )
  print(p)

  gp_multi_model = stan_model(file="gp-multi-fit.stan")

  gp_multi_fit <- sampling(
    gp_multi_model
    , data = list(
      N = length(y2)
      , D = 2
      , X = matrix(c(x2,group),nrow=length(x2),ncol=2,byrow=F)
      , Y = y2
    )
    , iter = 2000
    , chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1
    , pars = 'Sigma' #don't bother including Sigma in saved samples
    , include = FALSE #
  )
  alarm()
  print(gp_fit)

  #save(gp_multi_fit,file='gp_multi_fit.RData')
  y_preds = extract(
    gp_multi_fit
    , pars = 'y_preds'
  )[[1]]

  loci = apply(y_preds,2,quantile,prob=.025)
  hici = apply(y_preds,2,quantile,prob=.975)
  loci_a = loci[1:(ncol(y_preds)/2)]
  hici_a = hici[1:(ncol(y_preds)/2)]
  loci_b = loci[(ncol(y_preds)/2+1):ncol(y_preds)]
  hici_b = hici[(ncol(y_preds)/2+1):ncol(y_preds)]

  p = ggplot()
  p = p + geom_point(
      data = dat
      , mapping = aes(
          x = x
          , y = y
          , colour = as.character(group)
      )
      , alpha = .5
  )
  p = p + geom_ribbon(
      data = data.frame(
        x = x2[1:(length(x2)/2)]
        , ymin = loci_a
        , ymax = hici_a
        , group = '0.5'
      )
      , mapping = aes(
        x = x
        , ymin = ymin
        , ymax = ymax
        , fill = group
      )
      , alpha = .5
  )
  p = p + geom_ribbon(
      data = data.frame(
        x = x2[1:(length(x2)/2)]
        , ymin = loci_b
        , ymax = hici_b
        , group = '-0.5'
      )
      , mapping = aes(
        x = x
        , ymin = ymin
        , ymax = ymax
        , fill = group
      )
      , alpha = .5
  )
  print(p)
